facts.text: Dubai began as a pearling and fishing settlement in the early 18th century, then blossomed into a regional trade hub after declaring itself a free port in 1901 and extending the Creek in 1961.
Dubai Creek sustained the city’s community life and was the original engine behind its economic boom.
Dubai Marina’s story started in the early 2000s as part of the emirate’s plan to expand its urban footprint and redefine waterfront living.
By the mid‑2000s Marina had become a thriving residential and commercial hub, thanks to landmarks like the Marina Promenade, Dubai Marina Mall, and Marina Walk.
Today Dubai Marina remains one of the city’s most sought‑after areas, prized for its lifestyle, amenities, proximity to major landmarks, and planned future developments.
Dubai was a British protectorate, with Britain handling foreign policy and defense under the 1892 Exclusive Agreement that bound the Trucial States.
